solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expert composer making records

parts.note: arch can mean expert or highly skilled, as in an arch exponent
Charles Ives was an American composer

explanation.surface: A skilled composer is busy cutting records in a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' tempts as music recordings; here it means stored documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents, so records kept for posterity.

clue.text: One breaking step showing remorse

indicators.note: the numeral breaking into the ladder step means it goes inside it

parts.note: a rung is a step on a ladder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who has broken a stair is sorry about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing is regretting, so the participle describes someone feeling remorse.

clue.text: Pineapple and some bananas eaten (not "ate") in class

parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas growing together

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed inside the word for class

parts.note: a grade is a class or level

indicators.note: the instruction says to remove those three letters from the word eaten

explanation.surface: A fruity scene: pineapple and bananas being eaten in a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand of bananas is a bunch; 'Pineapple' is soldiers' slang, not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple is soldiers' slang for a hand grenade, from its segmented casing resembling the fruit.

clue.text: Corruptly closing river in the season

indicators.note: the adverb closes around the river abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: venally means in a corrupt, bribable way

explanation.surface: Something done corruptly as a river closes for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernally means in spring, a particular season of the year.

clue.text: Not quite clear paper's to turn up, organised extra books

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the newspaper's name from bottom to top

parts.note: The Times is the newspaper; the 's reads as 'is'
ran, as in ran an event, means organised
spare means extra, additional
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An instruction about a newspaper being turned over and extra books arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses TIMES to SEMIT; the self-referential paper is The Times itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Semitransparent means partly see-through, so translucent rather than fully clear.

clue.text: Defeated, have to amputate

definitions.meaning: to see off, past tense ..., means to defeat an opponent
to ... a limb is to cut it off

explanation.surface: Beaten, a patient must have a limb removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saw off works both as the past of see off (beat) and as cutting off with a saw.

clue.text: Way to include member of large family in cast

indicators.note: the street abbreviation is made to include the other piece within it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a quin is one of quintuplets, five siblings born together

explanation.surface: A way to fit one of a big family into a theatrical cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors; it is a cast in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A squint is a misalignment of the eyes, also called a cast.

clue.text: Wilde for one with a certain appeal

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with; that the answer's letters also sit in this word is a coincidence
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde described as a man with a certain charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was famed for clever humour, so he is an example of a wit.

clue.text: Soldiers in fracas on royal ship

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the word for a brawl

parts.note: a fracas is a fight
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Troops get caught up in a brawl aboard a royal vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: Finally fed such a man here?

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word fed is used here

parts.note: the inner man is a humorous term for the stomach or appetite, the man who is fed

explanation.surface: A man who has at last been fed asks whether this is the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such a man' points back to 'fed': the inner man is the one fed. The definition is loose, hence the question mark: dinner is where one is fed.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is fed at a meal, so the dinner is the occasion where that feeding happens.

clue.text: Doctor frees police up

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
unties means releases or frees

explanation.surface: A doctor releases police officers who were tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' belongs to the definition: up means on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, officers famously on horseback.

clue.text: A mythical giant with eyes on stalks

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, paired with Magog

explanation.surface: A legendary giant stares with bulging eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited, the state of someone staring wide-eyed.

clue.text: First law by Confucius, say: show maturity

parts.note: a law is an act, so the first one is act one
Confucius is an example of a sage, a wise man

explanation.surface: The first rule from Confucius: behave like a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To act one's age is to behave as befits one's years, displaying maturity.

clue.text: Act confused, failing pass

indicators.note: the words failing to stay in order signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor confused about failing an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'failing' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe conduct is a document guaranteeing free passage, a kind of pass.

clue.text: One in bed appeared to have a bad back

parts.note: came means arrived or appeared

indicators.note: the words a bad are read backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A patient in bed seemed to have a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in bed' suggests a patient; it is a plant in a flower bed. 'back' reverses A ILL to LLIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is a flowering shrub, the sort of plant grown in a garden bed.

clue.text: Beauty's first seen in a sublime ruined temple site

indicators.note: the initial letter is seen inside the rearranged letters
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of sublime are jumbled
only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A beautiful sight in a magnificent ruined temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles A SUBLIME, and B from 'Beauty's first' goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Simbel in Egypt is the site of rock-cut temples of Ramesses II.

clue.text: One from dairy chain picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a fetter is a chain or shackle

explanation.surface: Something from a dairy chain store is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dairy chain' reads as a shop chain; 'chain' is the fetter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a Greek cheese, a product of the dairy.

clue.text: Perhaps one burgling home more loyal daughter interrupts

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the daughter abbreviation breaks into the comparative

parts.note: truer means more faithful or loyal

explanation.surface: A loyal daughter disturbs a burglar at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is one example of a trespasser who breaks into a place uninvited.

clue.text: Getting back, have left bed for cat

indicators.note: the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: I am up means I have left bed, giving am up

explanation.surface: Returning home, the cat has got out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a large American wild feline.

clue.text: Without French priest, one's paid for nothing

parts.note: sine is Latin for without
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: Lacking a French priest, someone gets paid for doing no work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work.

clue.text: On diary confirm date, at first not offering money

parts.note: to ink in an appointment is to confirm it in a diary in pen

indicators.note: only the opening letter of date is taken

explanation.surface: Confirming a date in a diary without offering payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in kind means settling with goods or services instead of cash.

clue.text: Two kids: pa and I grip one roughly

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged roughly, not in their order

explanation.surface: Dad and I clutch one of the two children roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon pair is a family of one boy and one girl, or boy-girl twins.

clue.text: Head in various directions

parts.note: two different compass points, north and east, give the first pair
two more compass points, south and south, complete the head

explanation.surface: A head pointing every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland, a promontory, as in Loch Ness's shores or Dungeness.

clue.text: Hot dish eaten by psalmist

indicators.note: the answer is swallowed inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A psalm-writer eats a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich stew of game birds, served as a hot dish.

clue.text: Give most important backing in a live case

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the verb meaning to live

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: the word for most important is read backwards

parts.note: vital means most important, essential

explanation.surface: Give a key cause your support in a live court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the word for most important, and 'in' puts it inside BE. 'Give' plays no part in the wordplay; the blog also finds it redundant.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, used for by, with or from.

clue.text: Answer very quietly; one may be on the phone

definitions.text: one may be on the phone

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical notation for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone answering the phone in a whisper.
explanation.definitionFit: An app is a software application, the sort installed on a smartphone.

clue.text: Fetch strong drink

definitions.meaning: a fetch is an apparition or ... of a living person

explanation.surface: Go and get a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Double means both a spectral lookalike and a two-measure serving of spirits.

clue.text: Like a ski-run? Work in transport in winter

indicators.note: the work abbreviation is placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is transport over snow
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A wintry job running a ski resort's transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-run descends a hillside, so it is inclined or sloping.

clue.text: Go back and prepare to run

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in your turn
the tail is the back end of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to retreat and get ready to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back' reads as one phrase meaning retreat, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to turn round and flee, the move made before running away.
